content:
The Custer County Courthouse is located in Custer, South Dakota. It was built in 1885 and is the oldest standing courthouse in South Dakota. The courthouse is a two-story building made of native sandstone, and features Italianate and Romanesque architectural styles.

The courthouse is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and has been carefully restored to preserve its historic charm. It is still in use today as the main courthouse for Custer County, housing courtrooms and administrative offices.

The courthouse is notable for being a popular tourist attraction in Custer due to its historic significance and unique architecture. Visitors can tour the courthouse and learn about its history, as well as explore the surrounding area which is known for its natural beauty and outdoor recreation opportunities.
